item.title: Ducks land in CFP rankings despite rocky season
item.description: Oregon football’s season hasn’t worked out the way it expected. But the Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) were ranked in the first College Football Playoff rankings. Oregon came in at No. 23 in the initial rankings, revealed live on ESPN on Tuesday. Dan Lanning’s team is on the outside looking in at the 12-team playoff, one season before a 24-team playoff is set to likely go into effect. The No. 23 Ducks are coming off a confidence-boosting win over Northwestern, heading on the road to face No. 12 Ohio State (6-2, 4-1) this Saturday. That matchup originally included the preseason Nos. 1 and 2 teams in the AP poll. But in this chaotic college football season, the Buckeyes are reeling after a road loss to No. 20 USC. Other Big Ten teams in this week’s CFP rankings include No. 19 Iowa, No. 8 UCLA and No. 4 Indiana. item.title: Ravens RB Derrick Henry instantly shuts down trade noise after Jaguars rout
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Ravens RB Derrick Henry instantly shuts down trade noise after Jaguars rout appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Derrick Henry and the Baltimore Ravens suffered another ugly loss on Thursday night, this time falling 33-10 to the Jacksonville Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium . Amid growing chatter about his future, the star running back made it clear he is not thinking about going anywhere . Henry was asked after the game whether he expects to remain with the team for the rest of the season, given Baltimore’s struggles. He quickly shut down the idea . “I’m not mentioning me going anywhere else. I’m saying let’s go back to work, try to get better and turn this around,” Henry said, via Cordell Woodland. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The question came after ESPN’s Dan Graziano flagged Henry as “someone to keep an eye on” ahead of the trade deadline. The 32-year-old turns 33 in January and is set to earn $12 million next season, none of which is guaranteed. It has been a frustrating stretch for Henry and the Ravens. Baltimore has now lost four straight games, dropping to 4-5 and last place in the AFC North. Injuries have played a major role, with both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley landing on injured reserve. That forced undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his first career start on just three days’ rest, and he completed 10 of 18 passes for 60 yards with two interceptions. Henry’s own struggles continued. He finished with 57 yards on 17 carries and took 10 direct snaps, marking his fourth straight game with fewer than 60 rushing yards. Justice Hill provided Baltimore’s lone touchdown with a 65-yard run in the fourth quarter, with the game already out of reach. Still, Henry made some history in the loss. He passed both Jerome Bettis and LaDainian Tomlinson to move into seventh place on the NFL’s all-time rushing list , with Curtis Martin next in his sights. Meanwhile, the Jaguars improved to 6-2 behind a balanced effort. Trevor Lawrence connected with Parker Washington on a 50-yard touchdown before halftime, and Cam Little knocked down four field goals. The Ravens will have extra time to regroup before hosting the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football on Nov. 16. Henry’s comments suggest he wants to be part of the turnaround, but Baltimore’s front office could face some tough decisions if the losing continues. item.title: A Scottish influence has transformed New Zealand – but can they finally beat the All Blacks?
item.description: The New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie took plenty from his three years at the Glasgow Warriors but it is the chuckles that he remembers most fondly. “The Scottish are funny people and I haven't laughed as much in any environment as much as I have in my time here,” Rennie explained back in 2020 after embarking on what proved an ill-fated stint with Australia. “I've loved the people and I've loved our time here. It's been special, we'll miss it.” Dave Rennie spent three years at Glasgow (Getty) Perhaps it is no surprise, then, that there has been such a strong Scottish influence at the heart of his project to restore the All Blacks ’ spirit. Mike Blair won 85 caps at scrum half and captained Scotland 14 times; until deciding he rather preferred life overseeing attack, it appeared he was being groomed as Gregor Townsend ’s successor in the highest coaching office in the land. Instead, he and Rennie return to Murrayfield with a New Zealand side in a phase of reinvention or rediscovery – re-finding the tenets that made them great and forging perhaps the world’s most outstanding attack. It has proved a natural fit. Blair has admitted to feeling a degree of impostor syndrome when he first came into All Blacks camp earlier this year, but has found the squad highly receptive to his methods. He has done excellent work, too, getting a tune out of a series of playmakers and associated parts through a demanding itinerary. Unbeaten so far in the Nations Championship having overcome France, Italy and Ireland in July, they carry confidence from two professional performances against the Wallabies last month. “We're in a good place, I think,” Blair said this week. “We’re pleased with what we did against Australia but we're also aware that playing Scotland at Murrayfield is a really big challenge. It's another good opportunity to show the growth in our game.” Scotland struggled to get close to New Zealand during the playing days of Mike Blair (far left) (Getty) The former scrum half made a self-deprecating crack that he’d already contributed to a few All Blacks wins over Scotland this week but his own playing days do serve as a reminder of how this challenge has changed for the tourists. Back when their attack coach wore the thistle, the result was a foregone conclusion; in four meetings with the All Blacks as a player, Blair only got within 20 points once. "When I played, New Zealand played their second-string team. They gave guys opportunity against us," he admitted. ”Times have changed from that.” The last four meetings have been decided by eight points or fewer. item.title: ‘Been cheating’- Chiefs fans face fiery response over Patrick Mahomes and controversial call
item.description: Photo by William Purnell/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Former Denver Broncos safety Justin Simmons has hit back at Kansas City Chiefs fans questioning the controversial false start call that helped decide their team’s defeat. The Chiefs appeared to have snatched a late victory against Denver after Patrick Mahomes found the end zone in the final seconds. However, a false start penalty on Jaylon Moore wiped out the touchdown before Kansas City eventually lost 28-24. Chiefs supporters were quick to question the decision, but Simmons has little sympathy for their complaints and believes the officials made the right call. Justin Simmons accuses Kansas City Chiefs of benefiting from refereeing decisions Speaking on DNVR Sports’ The Last Line with J.Simms + K. Jack , Simmons launched into a fiery response to the criticism from Kansas City fans. He said: “I seen it all on social media and I already got beef with Chiefs fans anyway. That wasn’t a false start. They call that on us. They hate us… My rant? Y’all been cheating y’all whole time y’all had Patrick Mahomes. That’s my rant. Refs been cheating for y’all.” Simmons also took issue with the amount of attention Mahomes receives, even when the Chiefs are not playing. “I’m watching Sunday Night Football when I hear, ‘You know, this guy reminds me of? Number 15 in Kansas City, Patrick Mahomes.’ And we’re not even watching the Chiefs. We’re watching the New York Giants versus the Dallas Cowboys. And I gotta hear about Patrick Mahomes.” He then doubled down on his criticism of the fanbase, insisting the penalty was justified. “My rant is at the Chiefs fans that are delusional enough to think that that was not a false start. It was. Y’all lost. And y’all lost at the one-yard line. Ha!” The controversy centred on Moore moving his right foot after turning his head to look at Mahomes. A Broncos linebacker pointed out the movement, and officials ruled it a false start. Head coach Andy Reid disagreed with the decision, while Mahomes admitted he had not seen the replay but accepted the officials’ call. However, Simmons and former Broncos teammate Kareem Jackson have both defended the referees. For Kansas City, the missed opportunity proved costly, with Malcolm Roach sacking Mahomes on the ensuing fourth-down attempt to seal Denver’s 28-24 win. item.description: Fernando Forestieri has gone from playing in the top leagues in Italy and Spain to signing for Oxford City [Oxford City] A Saturday afternoon in October at the Hebburn Sports and Social Ground, Tyne & Wear. Some Hebburn Town fans are already heading for the exits as Oxford City, 3-0 up in the 81st minute, send on their new signing. Fernando Forestieri has shared pitches with Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo and Zlatan Ibrahimovic, and played in front 72,000 fans at Real Madrid's iconic Bernabeu Stadium. On this occasion, down in English football's sixth tier, there are 873 supporters present to witness Oxford City's new Argentine number 15 come on for his debut. "It was like a tennis match, the ball going one way one second, then the other way the next," Forestieri, 36, told BBC Sport after his new club, nicknamed the Hoops, secured a seventh win in 11 games to sit third in National League North. On Friday, Oxford City host Leicester City in the first round of the FA Cup (19:45 GMT), with former Watford and Sheffield Wednesday forward Forestieri looking to inspire the non-league club to a famous win over the League One Foxes. It is 10 years since Leicester famously won the Premier League title. In the same season Forestieri was helping Sheffield Wednesday reach the Championship play-off final, where the Owls lost to Hull City at Wembley. "There's a big gap between what Leicester did 10 years ago and where they are now," he said. "Why can't Oxford City cause an upset? This is what the FA Cup is all about." Forestieri ready for fresh challenge at Oxford City Forestieri encountered Barcelona, Messi and Ibrahimovic while playing for Malaga in Spain's top flight in 2009-10. Meanwhile, he shared the same pitch with Ronaldo as recently as five years ago when Juventus played Forestieri's Udinese team in Serie A. "You never forget being on the same pitch as these big players," added Forestieri, whose CV includes scoring against Inter Milan for Siena in 2008. "Messi, Ronaldo, Ibrahimovic... unbelievable skills. "I'm very lucky. Being that close to them you remember their first touch, their vision." Forestieri grew up playing football on the streets of Rosario - the same city in Argentina Messi was born - and idolised Diego Maradona. When Maradona died in 2020, Forestieri wrote a tribute to the 1986 Argentina World Cup winner on the back of his Udinese shirt. "Growing up in Argentina, everyone pretended to be Diego," he said. It was an issue that was apparent to everyone. “There are well-documented reasons why the Braves were in the market for a frontline starter at the Trade Deadline. Though they added a depth piece in Tyler Mahle, they didn't land the type of clear difference-maker that many fans wanted. As the team heads down the stretch, there's now even more scrutiny on a few things: the lack of a potent 1-2 punch for the postseason, their bullpen's durability and the rotation's overall dependability," MLB.com's Jason Foster wrote. Now, heading into 2027, Atlanta faces similar questions about the stability of its pitching rotation. “While it wasn't their downfall in the end, the starting rotation has been a constant thorn in the Atlanta Braves' side for multiple seasons now. For 2026, it was no different. As the page turns to 2027, it's to see how it shakes up. There will be at least one guarantee. Chris Sale is the ace. Gray is dependable as they come, being one of just six pitchers to hurl at least 160 innings in each of the last four seasons. The wily veteran has shown a propensity for pitching in a variety of different environments, and though his strikeout numbers shrank last season, he hasn’t logged a below-average FIP since 2016. The question is when Father Time will catch up with him,” Laws wrote. Gray was dominant in 2026, leading all of MLB with 18 wins. The right-hander has pitched for several teams throughout his career, including the New York Yankees . Gray recently completed his $75 million contract with the Boston Red Sox. item.title: Ireland vs Argentina offers tantalising World Cup preview to kick off huge autumn
item.description: World Cup quarter-final. Six syllables to chill the bones of any Ireland rugby fan. A peak seemingly so impossible to summit that it makes Mount Everest look like Slieve Donard. Ireland’s dismal record in rugby’s global showpiece scarcely needs repeating – but we’ll do so anyway. In the 10 editions of the World Cup to date, the Irish have been knocked out in the quarter-finals a ludicrous eight times, the short-lived quarter-final play-off once and the pool stage once. They simply cannot reach the semi-finals. It doesn’t matter whether they enter as a plucky underdog (1987 – lost 33-15 to Australia) or the No 1-ranked side in the world (2019 – beaten 46-14 by New Zealand ); whether they’ve downed a southern hemisphere giant to top their pool (2023 – lost 28-24 to the All Blacks after 37 phases of agony ) or have scraped through the groups in second spot (1995 – lost 36-12 to France), the result is the same. Ireland have endured World Cup heartbreak time and time again (PA) Sometimes it’s one-sided (2003 – beaten 43-21 by Les Bleus, having trailed 27-0 at half-time) and sometimes it’s agonising (1991 – lost 19-18 to Australia thanks to Michael Lynagh’s 80th-minute try in the corner) but it’s always a last-eight exit. But why are we talking about Ireland’s World Cup wobbles when there is almost a year to go until the latest edition in Australia? Because the very first game of this autumn’s Nations Championship is set to give us a tantalising preview of what could be to come in 12 months’ time. If everything goes to seeding (a big if, granted..), with both teams topping their pool and negotiating an eminently winnable last-16 clash, then on 31 October 2027 in Brisbane, Ireland and Argentina will do battle in a Rugby World Cup quarter-final. And this Friday night in Dublin, those same teams will try lay down a psychological marker, while kickstarting their autumn in style. Joe McCarthy scored a try when Ireland won the last game between the sides in 2024 (PA) Juan Cruz Mallia is one of Argentina’s game-breaking options (PA) Ireland will be confident. After a 36-14 defeat in Paris to begin the 2026 Six Nations, they reeled off four straight wins to finish second in the table, and only missed out on the title due to Thomas Ramos’s 83rd-minute penalty against England on Super Saturday, before beating Australia and Japan away from home in the summer. item.title: Syracuse’s Gerry McNamara Peels Back Curtain On Gavin Doty, Mark Morano
item.description: GREENVILLE, SOUTH CAROLINA - MARCH 18: Gavin Doty #4 of the Siena Saints speaks with the media during practice day ahead of the first round of the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament at Bon Secours Wellness Arena on March 18, 2026 in Greenville, South Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Getty The Syracuse Orange didn’t please new head coach Gerry McNamara with their season-opening win over New Haven earlier this week. G-Mac was happier after their Thursday night win over Central Connecticut State. McNamara is always going to find moments where SU can improve, but he felt Syracuse was closer to its best self on Thursday. The score certainly looks a lot better — Syracuse won 102-49. It was a balanced effort from the Orange, too. Gavin Doty led the way with 18 points. Mark Morano had 16 points. Luke Wilson had 14 points from his center position. Sadiq White put up 8 points with 10 rebounds. and Garwey Dual rounded out the starters with 8 points and 4 assists. Off the bench, Kiyan Anthony dropped 14 points for the Orange. Amarri Monroe and Tasman Goodrick each added 8 points off the bench themselves. Most notable after the game was the way McNamara talked about Doty and Morano. Gerry McNamara on Gavin Doty McNamara was asked “what it takes to get Gavin Doty’s motor going” in his postgame press conference. G-Mac laughed. “What does it take to get Gavin Doty’s motor going?” McNamara laughed. “Nothing. Nothing. He’s going to figure it out. I don’t have to do anything to get his motor going. He’s gonna play hard every second, every possession. He’s gonna find a way. There’s no telling Gav he’s not playing hard enough. There’s coaching him on certain things in terms of over-aggression sometimes. He’s gonna find something.” Doty came with McNamara from Siena, and it wasn’t immediately clear how he might translate. And sure, this isn’t ACC play at the moment. But right now, Doty looks like he belongs, and his motor helps that cause. Gerry McNamara on Mark Morano Morano hit three 3-pointers in the opener and hit four 3-pointers on Thursday night. That’s going to be his role in the Syracuse starting lineup, to be sure. “We ran a play for him and he didn’t shoot it, so I screamed at him,” McNamara said. “He’s a good player. Right at the start of the game he got downhill and made a layup. It’s undeniable he’s a really good offensive player. He can find the net. He’s bigger than you think. He’s a legit 6-6. The kid’s got big-time potential… He shoots the blood out of the ball, and I need him to shoot it when he’s open.” Morano came to Syracuse as a highly touted recruit from Slovenia. This is his first college basketball experience, and he’s off to a great start. item.title: Giants DC Dennard Wilson drops defiant truth bomb on holding his defense accountable
item.description: Denny Simmons / The Tennessean / USA TODAY NETWORK Giants DC Dennard Wilson drops defiant truth bomb on holding his defense accountable appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Dennard Wilson has not been shy about calling out the New York Giants ’ defense this season, and the defensive coordinator is not changing his approach as the team prepares to face the Philadelphia Eagles. Asked whether there is a danger in being so blunt publicly, Wilson did not flinch . “I think we get too caught up into not speaking the truth, right? The film doesn’t lie, and it never lies. And it’s always evidence. It’s a solid tape. And what I said in front of this podium, they’ve heard me say it from the first day they were here. So it’s nothing that they haven’t heard before,” Wilson said, via SNY. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Dennard Wilson talks about holding himself and his defense accountable: "We get too caught up in not speaking the truth. The film doesn't lie…too many coaches these days are scared to have those hard conversations" pic.twitter.com/5OOKpo14dQ — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) November 5, 2026 “It’s not calling out a specific player. It’s calling out a behavior. It’s calling out what we’re not doing collectively, because at the end of the day, it’s me as well. So if I let it slip, shame on me,” he continued. “You know, I think too many coaches these days are scared to have those hard conversations.” Wilson added that a strong bond with his players is what allows him to be so direct. “If you build a relationship and you have this bond and you have this tight-knit group, you can speak to them in a certain way and identify certain things without attacking them personally. It’s not a personal attack. It’s a behavioral attack,” Wilson said. “And that’s how I go about it, and that’s how I’ve been trained to do this since I was a young coach 20-some years ago.” Wilson made headlines last month after a Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints, when the Giants missed 18 tackles. item.description: George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty There have been a significant numbers of explanations to emanate from The Star in recent weeks to explain the relative drop in production from Dallas Cowboys star receiver George Pickens this season. Pickens was the talk of the NFL last season, when he was dealt from Pittsburgh and broke out with 93 catches and 1,429 yards receiving, the fourth-most in a single season in Cowboys history. This year, the numbers are down, and the Cowboys have suggested that is because teams are double-teaming him, because he has a hamstring injury and because Dak Prescott has simply found fellow star receiver CeeDee Lamb more often. But the counterpoint has been made, too, whether it’s to coach Brian Schottenheimer, owner Jerry Jones or EVP Stephen Jones: Other teams find a way to get the ball to their best playmakers, even if he is double-covered or even if someone else is open. Whatever the reason, the fact remains that the Cowboys don’t get the ball to Pickens enough. And they should change that. Klayton Adams Wants Cowboys to Get More George Pickens Going Now, for the first time, the call to get Pickens more involved is coming from inside the Cowboys house: Offensive coordinator Klayton Adams, who does not call the plays (Schottenheimer does), said on Thursday in his meeting with the media that Dallas should get Pickens more involved, and should do so earlier in games. Pickens, according to Todd Archer of ESPN, has two catches for 29 yards in the first quarter of the past five Cowboys games. Cowboys OC, Klayton Adams, speaks on the importance of what George Pickens has added to this offense since his arrival in Dallas. “Extremely. He’s a premium playmaker in the NFL. Boxing is, however, far from standing alone when it comes to conjuring up a fighting spirit. That stirring of emotions saw former world heavyweight champion Tyson earn the title of “baddest man on the planet”, with endless hours of sparring and bag work mapping out a course from the mean streets of Brooklyn to the bright lights of Las Vegas - success achieved by blending attitude and ability to achieve a seemingly impossible dream. Similar tales of rags being traded for riches can be found across the sporting spectrum, with football slotting neatly into that category. The high life is lived by many that started out in humble surroundings, with many of those dragging themselves to the top while absorbing some thunderous blows along the way - those of the variety that Tyson so eloquently spoke about. Football may be a team game, and boxing an individual pursuit, but there are plenty of blurred lines between the two and that goes a long way towards explaining why prominent figures on the pitch and in the ring are often intertwined. Societal roots Boxing and football boast working-class roots that helped both sports to grow Why are boxing and football so intrinsically linked? When it comes to skill sets, the two pastimes are worlds apart. One requires dexterity with the feet, the other mesmerising hand speed. There are few attributes, aside from maybe lightness on your toes, that could be considered transferable. This is not a bond based on visual appearance and individual talent, it is one rooted in societal structure and hierarchical class systems. item.description: Newcastle nightmare GFX - Getty/GOAL The St. James' Park outfit are on a miserable run, and it doesn't seem as if their manager has many ideas as to how to stop the rot "Matthias is one of the most exciting and highly regarded young coaches in football and I’m thrilled to welcome him to Newcastle United," Magpies CEO David Hopkinson said after Matthias Jaissle's arrival at St James' Park in early August. "We have conducted a thorough process, and he has emerged as the clear candidate for the role. He possesses all the qualities we were looking for. His track record of success, leadership qualities and relentless drive to improve make him an exceptional fit for Newcastle United. We believe he is the right person to lead the club into the next phase of our journey." Ross Wilson, Newcastle's sporting director, added: "His teams play high-energy football and we could feel his passion during all of our discussions throughout the recruitment process. He has consistently demonstrated an ability to improve players, build cohesive teams and create elite performance environments in his coaching career. His successes at [Red Bull] Salzburg and Al-Ahli underline his ability to deliver results while developing a clear football identity." Indeed, the 38-year-old delivered back-to-back Austrian Bundesliga and AFC Champions League titles at Salzburg and Al-Ahli, respectively, implementing a high-tempo brand of football that gave fans at both clubs value for money. But given his complete lack of top level coaching experience, Jaissle was a surprise choice to replace Eddie Howe, who stepped down in the summer after five years, one Carabao Cup success and two top-five Premier League finishes. There's little doubt that the selection process favoured Jaissle in at least some part because Al-Ahli and Newcastle share the same Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF) owners. The big billing from senior club officials did not mask the fact they were taking a big risk with Jaissle, and just three months into the 2026-27 campaign, it's looking like a major backfire. item.title: Why managers can learn a lot from leaders like Napoleon - Pulis
item.description: [BBC] The November international break is almost upon us, which always means one thing - the managerial merry-go-round is about to properly get into gear. It's known as 'sacking season' for a reason - the new campaign has started to take shape and I know from experience that any manager who is not winning games will always be sleeping with just one eye closed, and the other one open. At any club on a poor run of results, the owners and supporters will be questioning whether the manager is the right fit to continue. This two-week break from domestic games is the ideal opportunity to blood the new incumbent and give them a period of getting to know everyone before the games start up again. That means it is 'hiring season' too, but there are always far more out-of-work managers than vacant positions. Since the start of last season, 60 different managers have resigned or been sacked by teams in the Premier League and Football League. Three of them left to take up offers from other clubs but, in total, 37 of them - or 62% - are not currently in management. For most managers, it's rarely the case where you walk into a new club within a few weeks of leaving your last one, so what do out-of-work managers do between jobs to make sure they are ready to take the next opportunity that fits? 'Get your backside off the sofa' Known as 'The Bald Eagle', Jim Smith was renowned as a master of winning promotion during a management career that spanned almost 40 years. He is pictured here celebrating after leading Derby into the Premier League in 1996 [Getty Images] It is more than 32 years since I received my marching orders from my first job at Bournemouth, who were in what is now known as League One. I was devastated. I had - as I always did - given everything I could do to benefit the club, and with it being my first sacking I honestly did not know where my next step would take me. But, on the second day of me being out of work, my home phone rang and at the end of the line was Jim Smith, who was in charge of Portsmouth, a few miles down the south coast. I knew Jim then, but not really well. I'd been a manager for two years, but by then he had already spent 25 years in the dugout, at eight different clubs. He asked how I was and, before I could even reply, recited these immortal words, which always stuck with me - "son, you're not a real manager until you get sacked at least three times - so get your backside off the sofa and get on with getting another job" - then he put the phone down! I've used that sentence myself many times since to managers who have lost their job and are struggling to come to terms with it. That can happen a lot. People outside the game maybe don't realise how difficult it can be when you are sacked, and how it affects certain individuals differently - you can easily fall off the merry-go-round and, as a manager, you never know for sure whether you will get another chance. item.description: India's presidential palace, in smog, November 5, 2026 (Sajjad HUSSAIN) India's cricket board has moved an international match scheduled for December out of New Delhi because of "potential weather disruption", as air pollution levels surged in the city. Toxic air pollution in the megacity spiked on Friday to more than 25 times the World Health Organization's recommended daily limit, data from air monitors showed. The southeastern coastal city of Visakhapatnam will instead host the one-day international (ODI) match between India and Sri Lanka on December 13. The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) said the decision was made "in view of the potential weather disruption and the proposed renovation work" at the Delhi stadium. During winter pollution peaks, when colder air traps pollutants close to the ground, PM2.5 readings can exceed 800 micrograms per cubic metre -- more than 50 times the WHO's 24-hour guideline. Air pollution was linked to an estimated 17,188 deaths in Delhi in 2023, nearly 15 percent of the total, making it the city's biggest individual risk factor, an analysis by Finland-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) found. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports Mark Davis owns two professional sports teams in Las Vegas, and both the Raiders and the WNBA’s Aces have partnerships with sportsbook BetMGM. But that doesn’t mean he’s a big supporter of the gambling boom that has taken over the sports world. In a new interview, Davis said that he’s “not a fan” of sports betting, particularly the rise of prop bets on individual players and plays. Davis said he worries that the growing gambling industry could threaten the integrity of professional sports. Gambling’s Growing Role in Sports Sports betting has exploded across the country in recent years, and leagues have been happy to cash in through partnerships with sportsbooks. But that growth has also come with a string of scandals, especially when it comes to prop bets. In October 2025, the FBI arrested Portland Trail Blazers head coach Chauncey Billups and Miami Heat guard Terry Rozier in connection with federal gambling investigations. A month later, Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz were indicted over an alleged scheme involving bets on individual pitches. Leagues are also dealing with the rise of prediction markets, which let users trade contracts tied to the outcomes of sporting events. The NFL has been more cautious than other leagues, declining to partner with prediction market operators. “We think that there needs to be stronger regulations into the predictive markets,” NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell told CNBC Sport in September. “We don’t feel like we have to be first in this. We feel like we’re going to be right. And the best thing to do is to be patient and make sure that you keep the integrity of the game number 1.” The NFL also filed an amicus brief with the Supreme Court in October, arguing that prediction markets are a form of gambling and should be regulated by the states. ‘The Integrity of the Game’ Speaking with CNBC Sport’s Michael Ozanian, Davis made it clear that he has some serious concerns about where things are heading. “I’m not a fan per se of gambling on sports, especially the one-on-ones, the proposition types of betting,” Davis said, via CNBC . “I think the key thing is the integrity of the game,” he added. Davis, who moved the Raiders from Oakland to Las Vegas in 2020, said he remembers a time when the NFL took a much harder line on gambling. “I remember growing up that there was a big sign in the locker room as you walked out that door that said, ‘No gambling whatsoever,’ or there’s suspension or you’re out of the league,” Davis said. Mikhail Pocknett and Jamias Ferere led Gardner-Webb with 12 points apiece. The Runnin' Bulldogs were out shot just 61% to 33%. item.description: ‘Why Wasn’t He Talking Like That After Isaiah Stewart Ran Up on Him?’ ‘A Clown’ — NBA Fans Rip Draymond Green Over Dillon Brooks ‘Villain’ Criticism Draymond Green isn’t backing down from the sequence that got him ejected from the Golden State Warriors’ 116-113 win over the Phoenix Suns on Monday. He also had plenty to say about Dillon Brooks while explaining it. The Warriors forward revisited the incident on his podcast on Thursday after Brooks gave reporters his account of what happened at Chase Center, drawing criticism from fans over his comments. The Golden State veteran then threw him to the floor before grabbing Dillon Brooks by the jersey when he approached him. Officials assessed the Warriors forward two technical fouls, with the second coming as part of a double technical that Brooks also received. He was ejected with Golden State trailing 67-57, and the Suns made the ensuing technical free throw to extend their lead to 68-57. Golden State rallied without him to win 116-113. The 2017 Defensive Player of the Year gave his side of the story on “The Draymond Green Show,” beginning with Maluach before turning his attention to the Suns forward. “You must stand on that type of time as a big man; if you don’t, your paint get ran through, no rim protection cause there’s no respect after that. … Where the plot twist is like Dillon Brooks running up … you were trying to be the villain … and that type of energy will not ever be respected.” Brooks addressed the confrontation when he spoke to reporters after the game: “I was just trying to de-escalate the whole thing. … He did a lot there, fell down, and pushed him at the end of it. … He was just tweaking all game. Rosberg blamed Charles Leclerc for repeatedly causing incidents with his teammate and called on team principal Fred Vasseur to establish clear racing guidelines.
